formation.title: The Aztec Empire Rises
formation.text:
From the marshes of Lake Texcoco, the Mexica have built the greatest empire the Americas have ever seen. Tenochtitlan stands as the jewel of a realm stretching from sea to sea, its canals and causeways a testament to the genius of its people. Now, as the Huey Tlatoani proclaims dominion over all Mesoamerica, the empire must decide its path. Will the flower wars continue to forge an unbreakable warrior elite, expanding the empire's reach through martial glory? Or will the pochteca merchant-spies become the instruments of a new kind of power, one built on trade routes, tribute networks, and the flow of cacao rather than blood?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Let the Flower Wars rage eternal!

modifiers.name: Way of the Flower Wars
modifiers.text: The Aztec Empire has perfected the art of ritual warfare. Armies march not merely to conquer, but to prove the supremacy of Huitzilopochtli over all rivals. Every battlefield becomes a sacred ground where warriors earn glory through the capture of worthy opponents.

options.text: The pochteca shall be the sinews of empire.

modifiers.name: The Pochteca's Road
modifiers.text: The empire's long-distance merchants, the pochteca, have been elevated to the status of a pillar of state. Their caravans carry cacao, quetzal feathers, and obsidian to the farthest reaches of Mesoamerica, and their intelligence networks serve as the eyes and ears of the Huey Tlatoani.

advances.name: Chinampa Agriculture
advances.text: The floating gardens of the Valley of Mexico produce multiple harvests per year, feeding a population that rivals any in the world.

advances.name: Atlatl Tradition
advances.text: The spear-thrower has been a defining weapon of Mesoamerican warfare for millennia. Aztec atlatl-wielding skirmishers rain deadly projectiles on their enemies from beyond melee range.

advances.name: Tlachtli Ball Courts
advances.text: The ritual ball game serves both religious and political functions, resolving disputes between cities and honouring the gods through athletic contest.

advances.name: Pochteca Trade Network
advances.text: The pochteca long-distance merchants maintain trade routes spanning all of Mesoamerica, dealing in luxury goods and serving as the empire's intelligence gatherers.

advances.name: Aqueduct Engineering
advances.text: Twin aqueducts carry fresh water from Chapultepec springs to the island city of Tenochtitlan, an engineering marvel that sustains a population of over 200,000.

advances.name: Obsidian Mastery
advances.text: Aztec craftsmen produce weapons, tools, and mirrors from volcanic obsidian with extraordinary skill. The macuahuitl, an obsidian-edged wooden sword, can decapitate a horse.

advances.name: Calpulli Organisation
advances.text: The calpulli, clan-based wards that form the administrative backbone of Aztec cities, coordinate taxation, land use, education, and military conscription at the local level.

advances.name: Order of the Cuachicqueh
advances.text: The Shorn Ones are the supreme warrior elite of the Aztec Empire. They swear never to retreat and always lead the vanguard in battle.

event.title: The Oath of the Shorn Ones
event.text: A new generation of the Cuachicqueh, the Shorn Ones, has completed their initiation rites. These elite warriors shave their heads, leaving only a single lock over the left ear, and paint one half of their face blue and the other half red or yellow. They swear before the gods that they will never retreat from battle, never take a step backward. In war, they are always the first to engage the enemy and the last to leave the field. Their oath is absolute: victory or death, with no middle ground. The other warrior orders, the Jaguar Knights and Eagle Warriors, look to the Cuachicqueh as the ultimate expression of martial devotion. Their presence on the battlefield stiffens the resolve of every warrior in the army.

options.text: Their oath binds them, and inspires us all.

modifiers.name: Ascendancy of the Shorn Ones
modifiers.text: The Cuachicqueh, warriors who have sworn to never take a step backward in battle, have become the living embodiment of Aztec martial virtue. Their painted faces and shaven heads strike terror into every foe.

advances.name: Flower Wars Doctrine
advances.text: The xochiyaoyotl, Flower Wars, are ritual conflicts that keep warriors sharp, provide captives for sacrifice, and demonstrate the empire's martial superiority without requiring total conquest.

advances.name: Tribute Administration
advances.text: A bureaucracy of calpixque (tribute collectors) ensures the steady flow of goods from over four hundred subject altepetl to the imperial treasury.

advances.name: Codex Tradition
advances.text: Aztec scribes, the tlacuiloque, create elaborate painted codices recording everything from astronomical observations to tribute assessments and herbal medicine.

event.title: The Great Codex Project
event.text: The scribes of the calmecac have undertaken an ambitious project: the systematic compilation of all Aztec knowledge into a comprehensive series of codices. Using amate bark paper and vibrant mineral pigments, the tlacuiloque, professional scribe-painters, record the empire's accumulated wisdom. Tonalamatl almanacs chart the sacred calendar and its rituals. Tribute rolls catalogue the exact obligations of every subject altepetl. Herbal codices document hundreds of medicinal plants, their preparation, and their uses, knowledge that rivals anything in the Old World. Astronomical records track the movements of Venus, the Sun, and the Moon with extraordinary precision. This is not merely record-keeping. It is the creation of an intellectual infrastructure that will allow the empire's knowledge to be transmitted, debated, and expanded for generations.

options.text: Knowledge is the foundation of empire.

modifiers.name: Wisdom of the Codices
modifiers.text: The scribes of the empire have begun a systematic effort to record and preserve knowledge in painted codices, from astronomical observations to tribute rolls, from medicinal plants to genealogies of the ruling houses.

advances.name: Cacao Trade
advances.text: Cacao beans serve as both currency and luxury good throughout Mesoamerica. Control of the cacao trade gives the empire economic leverage over the entire region.

advances.name: Reformed Defenses
advances.text: The empire strengthens its border fortifications and garrison system, building teocalli-fortresses that combine defensive strength with religious significance.

advances.name: Nahuatl Imperialism
advances.text: Nahuatl language and culture are actively promoted throughout the empire's domains, binding subject peoples to the Aztec identity through shared language, religion, and custom.

advances.name: Coyote Runners
advances.text: Elite runners serve as the empire's rapid communication network and fast-moving raiding force, covering vast distances through the mountains and jungles of Mesoamerica.

advances.name: Military Reformation
advances.text: The traditional warrior order system is reformed to incorporate new tactical doctrines, discipline and formation replace individual heroics as the foundation of Aztec military power.

advances.name: Centralised Tribute Reform
advances.text: The tribute system is fundamentally reorganised under direct imperial administration, replacing the patchwork of local arrangements with a centralised bureaucracy.

event.title: Reform of the Tribute System
event.text: The Aztec tribute system has grown vast, over four hundred subject altepetl pay regular tribute to Tenochtitlan in goods ranging from cotton mantles and warrior costumes to cacao beans, gold dust, quetzal feathers, and jade. But the system is showing strain. Some provinces resist their assessments, others conceal their true wealth, and the logistics of collecting and storing tribute across such distances have become unwieldy. The Huey Tlatoani's advisors present two paths forward: tighten central control by replacing local tlatoque with imperial appointees who answer directly to Tenochtitlan, or formalize a compact that respects local autonomy in exchange for reliable tribute delivery and military commitment.

modifiers.name: Centralized Tribute Collection
modifiers.text: Imperial tribute collectors now answer directly to the Huey Tlatoani. Provincial governors are replaced by agents of the central administration, ensuring every bale of cotton, every load of cacao, and every consignment of obsidian reaches Tenochtitlan's coffers.

options.text: Let the altepetl govern themselves, so long as they pay.

modifiers.name: Federated Altepetl Compact
modifiers.text: Rather than imposing ever-heavier central control, the empire has formalized the autonomy of its constituent altepetl. Local tlatoque retain their authority in exchange for reliable tribute and military service, a system that breeds loyalty rather than resentment.

advances.name: Hydraulic Mastery
advances.text: Generations of experience with chinampas, aqueducts, and flood control have produced a class of hydraulic engineers without parallel in the Americas.

advances.name: Imperial Law Code
advances.text: A comprehensive legal code replaces the ad hoc rulings of individual tlatoque, providing consistent justice across the empire and strengthening central authority.

advances.name: Tlacochcalcatl Tradition
advances.text: Named after the Master of the House of Darts, these reformed imperial guards represent the pinnacle of Aztec military evolution, disciplined, well-equipped, and utterly loyal.

advances.name: Mesoamerican Renaissance
advances.text: A flowering of arts, sciences, and philosophy transforms the Aztec Empire into a centre of learning that draws on thousands of years of accumulated Mesoamerican civilisation.

event.title: A Mesoamerican Renaissance
event.text: Something remarkable is stirring in the Aztec Empire. The calmecac schools, once focused primarily on training priests and warriors, have become centres of broader intellectual inquiry. Nahuatl scholars debate philosophy, compose lyric poetry in the tradition of Nezahualcoyotl, and push the boundaries of astronomical knowledge. Artisans in Tenochtitlan produce goldwork, featherwork, and stone carving of breathtaking sophistication. Engineers continue to expand and refine the chinampa system and the city's hydraulic infrastructure. This flowering of culture and knowledge rivals anything the Old World has produced, a renaissance uniquely Mesoamerican in character, drawing on thousands of years of accumulated civilisation from the Olmec, Maya, Toltec, and now Aztec traditions.

options.text: The Fifth Sun illuminates a new age of learning.

advances.name: Modern Armies
advances.text: The Aztec military completes its transformation from a warrior-order system to a modern army with standardised equipment, tactical drilling, and professional officer corps.

advances.name: Trade Modernisation
advances.text: The ancient pochteca trade networks are modernised with new methods of accounting, credit, and warehousing, allowing Aztec commerce to compete with any nation.

advances.name: National Identity
advances.text: The diverse peoples of the empire (Nahua, Mixtec, Zapotec, Totonac, and dozens more) begin to forge a shared identity as citizens of the Aztec state.

advances.name: Industrial Dawn
advances.text: Aztec engineers and craftsmen apply their traditional ingenuity to new manufacturing techniques, beginning the transformation of the empire's economy from agrarian tribute to industrial production.

destiny.name: Destiny of the Aztec Empire
destiny.text: The Aztec Empire has been forged. Now the Huey Tlatoani must demonstrate that this realm can endure: that it is more than a passing shadow on the face of the Fifth Sun. Prove the empire's stability and the path forward shall reveal itself.

event.title: The Destiny of an Empire
event.text: The Aztec Empire stands at the threshold of a new age. Tenochtitlan, the island city of canals and causeways, is the beating heart of a realm that stretches from the Pacific shores to the Gulf coast. But the Huey Tlatoani's ambitions extend far beyond the boundaries of Mesoamerica. The gods demand more: more tribute, more glory, more proof that the Mexica are the chosen people of the Fifth Sun. The path chosen at the empire's founding now begins to bear fruit, and the destiny of the Aztec people awaits fulfilment.

options.text: The Fifth Sun shall never set.

destiny.name: Conquest of the Chichimecah
destiny.text: The wild northern frontier has long defied Aztec authority. The Chichimec peoples (nomadic hunters and raiders) must be brought to heel. The silver-rich lands of the Guachichil and the coastal settlements of Aridoamerica are seized to secure the empire's northern flank, and two subject lords pay tribute to Tenochtitlan.

conditions.text: Chose Way of the Flower Wars
Own Cuauchichil, or a subject owns it
Own Acaponeta, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Northern Frontier Falls
event.text: The Chichimec frontier (that vast, arid wilderness beyond the Valley of Mexico) has been the empire's great unfinished business for generations. Now it is finished. The Guachichil warriors, who once raided Aztec caravans with impunity, kneel before the Huey Tlatoani. The silver-bearing mountains of the north are ours, and the empire's flank is secure at last. The flower warriors who conquered these lands have proven that Aztec martial doctrine adapts to any terrain: desert, mountain, or jungle.

destiny.name: Empire of the Fifth Sun
destiny.text: With the north secured, the armies of the Fifth Sun march south into the highland kingdoms of Central America. Cuauhtemallan and the trading port of Naco must fall under Aztec dominion, and half of the Guatemalan highlands is held by the empire or its subject lords.

conditions.text: Own Cuauhtemallan, or a subject owns it
Own Naco, or a subject owns it
We or our subjects hold at least half of the locations of the Tezulutlan area

event.title: The March South
event.text: The armies of the Fifth Sun have swept through Central America. The highland fortress of Cuauhtemallan and the coastal trading hub of Naco both fly the Aztec standard. No power south of the Valley of Mexico can stand before the flower warriors. But how shall the empire consolidate these conquests? The war captains argue for constant readiness: the drums of war must never fall silent. But the temple priests counsel that these conquests should be consecrated to the gods, building sacred garrisons that bind conquered peoples through religious awe as much as military force.

options.text: Let the war drums thunder without cease.

modifiers.name: Thunder of the War Drums
modifiers.text: The war drums of the Aztec Empire sound without ceasing. The levies are swollen with eager warriors, and the cost of waging war has been reduced through constant practice. Every frontier province maintains its readiness for the next campaign.

modifiers.name: Sacred Conquest
modifiers.text: The conquered lands have been consecrated to Huitzilopochtli. Temple-fortresses garrison every major settlement, and the conquered peoples are drawn to the cult of the god who defeated their own. But sustaining armies across such vast territories takes its toll.

destiny.name: Lords of the Americas
destiny.text: The ultimate ambition: an empire spanning the entire American continent. The great chiefdom of Cofitachequi in the southeast and the ancient mound city of Cahokia in the heartland must both acknowledge Aztec supremacy, and five subject lords pay tribute. Only then can the Huey Tlatoani truly claim the title Lord of the Americas.

conditions.text: Own Cofitachequi, or a subject owns it
Own Cahokia, or a subject owns it

event.title: Lords of the Americas
event.text: It is done. The great chiefdom of Cofitachequi, famed for its pearls and copper, has submitted to Aztec authority. The ancient mound city of Cahokia (a place sacred to peoples the Mexica had never heard of a generation ago) now hosts an Aztec governor. The empire stretches from the frozen northern plains to the steaming jungles of the south. No realm in the Americas, and perhaps few in the entire world, can match the Aztec dominion in extent or power. The Huey Tlatoani must now decide how to project this unprecedented hegemony across such vast distances.

options.text: Our obsidian blades shall enforce our will.

modifiers.name: Obsidian Hegemony
modifiers.text: The reach of Aztec arms now extends across the continent. Tributary lords keep faith with Tenochtitlan, the levies of the provinces fight as hardened warriors, every battle adds to the army's renown, and the empire's colonial ambitions know no bounds.

options.text: We shall rule as the Sun rules: by radiance.

modifiers.name: Radiance of the Sun Lords
modifiers.text: The Aztec Empire governs through prestige and awe as much as through force. Mercenary companies from distant peoples serve the Huey Tlatoani, and foreign rulers seek alliance with the Sun Lords. But maintaining such a vast network of patronage is not without cost.

destiny.name: The Cacao Monopoly
destiny.text: Cacao beans are the currency and lifeblood of Mesoamerican trade. The pochteca must ensure that the empire's capital market controls the flow of this precious commodity. The treasury is filled and Tochtepec is built up, the town where the merchants keep their houses on the road to the cacao lands.

children.text: Cocoa is produced in the market
Cocoa is traded in the market

conditions.text: We own Tochtepec and its development is at least 6

event.title: The Cacao Kings
event.text: The pochteca have achieved something remarkable. Through a web of trade agreements, strategic purchases, and the occasional quietly eliminated rival, the Aztec Empire now controls the flow of cacao through its capital market. Every cup of xocolatl drunk from the Gulf coast to the Pacific shore enriches Tenochtitlan's coffers. The cacao bean, once merely a luxury beverage, has become the instrument of Aztec economic hegemony. The merchant princes of the pochteca guilds have earned their place alongside the warrior orders in the councils of the Huey Tlatoani.

options.text: Cacao flows like blood through our empire.

destiny.name: The Great Tianquiztli
destiny.text: The marketplace of Tlatelolco once amazed even the Spanish conquistadors. Now something greater still is built around it in Tenochtitlan: a continental trade network linking silver mines, cacao plantations, and luxury goods from every corner of the Americas.

conditions.text: A market the country is in

children.text: Silver is produced in the market
Silver is traded in the market

conditions.text: We own Tenochtitlan and its development is at least 24

event.title: The Continental Market
event.text: The tianquiztli of Tenochtitlan has become something the world has never seen before: a marketplace where goods from across an entire continent change hands. Silver from the northern mines, cacao from the tropical lowlands, obsidian from the volcanic highlands, and cotton from the coastal plains all flow through Aztec-controlled trade networks. The pochteca reckon their accounts in cacao beans and cotton cloth, a currency of their own that serves a uniquely Mesoamerican commercial vision. But how should this economic empire be governed?

options.text: The cacao lords shall guide our prosperity.

modifiers.name: Dominion of the Cacao Lords
modifiers.text: The pochteca merchant princes wield economic power that rivals any warrior order. Their networks rebuild war-torn provinces, and their diplomatic connections expand the empire's reach. But wealth breeds complacency.

options.text: Build ships and seek new markets beyond the sea.

modifiers.name: Ambition of the Market Kings
modifiers.text: The empire's commercial ambitions have turned seaward. Shipyards produce vessels to carry trade beyond the coastlines, and explorers chart new routes to distant markets. But the focus on trade comes at a cost to military readiness.

destiny.name: Merchants of the World
destiny.text: The pochteca have outgrown Mesoamerica. Their guilds were once those of twelve towns of the Valley; now Xicallanco, the port where they met the Maya traders, is the empire's own, the Caribbean trade routes are held through Habana, and the cacao heartlands of Chalchuapa are secured. The Aztec merchant class can project economic power across the entire known world.

conditions.text: Own Habana, or a subject owns it
Own Chalchuapa, or a subject owns it
Own Xicallanco, or a subject owns it

event.title: Merchants of the World
event.text: The pochteca have done what no Aztec ever dreamed possible. From their island in Lake Texcoco, they have built a commercial network that spans oceans and continents. Aztec trading posts dot the Caribbean. Cacao, obsidian, and featherwork flow outward; silver, fine cloth, and exotic luxuries flow back. The Huey Tlatoani must now decide how to channel this unprecedented wealth: shall the empire's roads carry settlers and administrators to found new provinces, or shall the merchant guilds hire foreign soldiers and sailors to protect and expand their ever-growing network?

options.text: Our people shall settle every road they walk.

modifiers.name: The Golden Roads
modifiers.text: Aztec settlers and administrators travel the empire's vast road network, establishing new provinces and integrating conquered peoples. Religious differences are no barrier to expansion: the empire's roads welcome all who submit to the Huey Tlatoani.

options.text: Let gold buy what obsidian cannot take.

modifiers.name: Empire of World Merchants
modifiers.text: The pochteca have become true world merchants, their commercial networks protected by hired soldiers and supported by a growing fleet. The empire's economic reach extends to every shore that Aztec ships can reach.

units.name: Cuachicqueh
units.text: The Shorn Ones, elite shock infantry who shave their heads and paint their faces, swearing before the gods never to retreat. They lead every charge and hold every line.

units.name: Atlatl Skirmisher
units.text: Levy warriors armed with the atlatl, an ancient spear-thrower that gives devastating range and striking power to even conscript troops.

units.name: Tlacochcalcatl Guard
units.text: Reformed imperial infantry named for the supreme military commander. These disciplined soldiers combine traditional Aztec ferocity with modern tactical formations.

units.name: Coyote Runner
units.text: Swift scouts and raiders who serve as the empire's rapid response force, crossing mountains and jungles with extraordinary speed.

buildings.name: Tlachtli Ball Court
buildings.text: A stone court for the ritual ball game that serves both religious devotion and political diplomacy, settling disputes between altepetl through sacred athletic contest.

buildings.name: Chinampa Terrace
buildings.text: Beds of lake mud piled between reed walls and staked with willow, cut through by canals that carry the canoes. Cropped several times a year, they raise far more maize than the dry fields around them and feed the cities of the lake.

where.text: The location's raw material is Maize

buildings.name: Pochteca Warehouse
buildings.text: A secure storehouse where the pochteca long-distance merchants inventory and redistribute goods, from cacao and quetzal feathers to obsidian and fine cloth.

buildings.name: Aztec Aqueduct
buildings.text: A stone channel bringing fresh water from highland springs, sustaining the population and health of Aztec cities built on lake islands.

buildings.name: Obsidian Workshop
buildings.text: A workshop where master craftsmen produce macuahuitl swords, arrowheads, surgical tools, and mirrors from volcanic obsidian, Mesoamerica's equivalent of steel.

buildings.name: Tianquiztli Market
buildings.text: A grand marketplace where merchants trade everything from cacao beans and cotton mantles to jade ornaments and quetzal feathers. The tianquiztli of Tlatelolco drew tens of thousands of traders daily.

buildings.name: Nahuatl Academy
buildings.text: A centre of learning that extends the calmecac tradition into broader scholarship, training administrators, scribes, and scholars in law, history, philosophy, and the natural sciences.

buildings.name: Teocalli Fortress
buildings.text: A fortified temple-complex that combines the sacred authority of the gods with the practical strength of stone walls and garrison quarters. These strongpoints anchor the empire's defenses.

buildings.name: Mesoamerican Manufactory
buildings.text: A workshop complex where traditional Aztec craftsmanship meets new production methods, producing textiles, obsidian tools, ceramics, and metalwork at industrial scale.

buildings.name: Sun Temple Complex
buildings.text: A grand temple-fortress complex dedicated to Huitzilopochtli, combining the sacred authority of the war god with the practical strength of an imperial garrison. The greatest such complex outside Tenochtitlan itself.

buildings.name: Pochteca Palace
buildings.text: A magnificent trading headquarters where the pochteca merchant princes coordinate the empire's vast commercial network. Warehouses, counting houses, and diplomatic reception halls surround a central market courtyard.

list.name: Excan Tlatoloyan
list.text: After the destruction of Azcapotzalco in 1428, Itzcoatl of Tenochtitlan, Nezahualcoyotl of Tetzcoco, and Totoquilhuaztli of Tlacopan agreed to share imperial tribute on a 2:2:1 ratio and to coordinate campaigns. The senior partner Tenochtitlan presided, but Tetzcoco's law-courts and Tlacopan's army contingents were independently administered. The alliance held for ninety years, projecting Mexica power from the Pacific to the Gulf. When the partners drifted, tributary towns sensed weakness and the perimeter unraveled.

list.name: Calpixque Service
list.text: The calpixque ('those who watch over') were imperial overseers stationed in conquered towns to keep the tribute rolls. The Codex Mendoza preserves the schedule: each of the thirty-eight tributary provinces delivered fixed quantities of cotton mantles, cacao beans, quetzal feathers, gold dust, lime, copal, and warriors twice a year. The calpixqui forwarded goods to Tenochtitlan, recorded shortfalls, and called punitive expeditions when payment lapsed. A diligent service enriched the throne; a lax one let provinces skim until tribute became fictional.

list.name: Pochteca Guild
list.text: The pochteca were the long-distance merchant brotherhood of Tlatelolco, organized in twelve great cities and answerable to their own tribunal at the Tlatelolco market, the largest in the Americas. They carried obsidian, cacao, gold ornaments, and quetzal feathers from Soconusco to the Gulf coast in armed caravans. A specialized branch, the naualoztomeca or 'disguised merchants', reported on unconquered lands while trading in them; their intelligence justified subsequent imperial campaigns. Their wealth let them buy the costume of nobility, which the hereditary pipiltin bitterly resented.

list.name: Calmecac Schools
list.text: The calmecac were the priestly academies attached to each major temple, where boys of pipiltin rank and selected commoner children entered as small children. They learned the picture-writing of the codices, the divinatory tonalpohualli calendar, oratory in the polished huehuetlatolli register, the histories, and the disciplines of fasting and self-mortification. Calmecac graduates filled the priesthoods, the high judiciary, and the captain-general ranks; under Tlacaelel's reforms they became the empire's official producer of literate elites. Their prestige insulated them from court politics, and a complacent priest-noble class could close ranks against outsiders.

list.name: Calpulli Wards
list.text: The calpulli were the ward-clan units of Tenochtitlan and the tributary altepetl: collective landholders whose elders allocated milpa to member households, sent boys to the telpochcalli (the commoner military school), fielded a labour-rotation gang for state corvee on the chinampas and the causeways, and represented their members in court. Each calpulli kept its own temple and patron. Calpulli was the bedrock of Mexica civic life and the recruiting ground of the imperial army; well-tended wards filled the quotas, while neglected ones fragmented into feuding lineages over scarce milpa.

list.name: Cuauhpipiltin Orders
list.text: The eagle and jaguar warriors (cuauhpipiltin, 'eagle-nobles') formed the empire's elite military meritocracy. A commoner who took four enemy captives in single combat was raised to cuauhpilli with the right to wear cotton, drink octli, dine in the royal palace, and own land in his own name. Moctezuma I codified the captive-quota ranks; Tlacaelel made the orders a permanent counterweight to the hereditary pipiltin. They led the empire's most ferocious assaults; in decline they degenerated into status-hungry captive-hunters who skirmished for individual glory while the cohort dissolved around them.

list.name: Tlatocan Council
list.text: The Tlatocan was the supreme council seated beside the huey tlatoani at Tenochtitlan, comprising the cihuacoatl (chief minister and de facto vizier), the tlacochcalcatl and tlacateccatl (the two captains-general), the great priests, and the senior pipiltin lords. It elected each new tlatoani from among the royal lineage on the death of his predecessor and sat in judgment on high crimes. Strong tlatoque (Itzcoatl with Tlacaelel, Moctezuma I, Ahuitzotl) bent the council to their will; weaker ones were managed by it, and a divided Tlatocan could paralyze the throne with factional intrigue.
